title: Integral finite presentations give the internal constructible scalar image
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite normed field extension, put $A=\mathcal O_E$, and fix a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_T$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_T(V)=C(|V|,E)$. Use the canonical map $B_T\cong(V\mapsto C(|V|,A))\to E_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] and the specified encodings $\Phi_A,\Phi_E$ between internal coefficient modules and sectionwise modules [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding]. Internal integral coefficients are $A_T^c=p_T^*C(-,A)$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathcal I_T=\Dbc(T,A)$ be the full completed integral category, including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. For every $K\in\mathcal I_T$, its inverse derived encoding $D(\Phi_A)^{-1}K$ is bounded, and each cohomology sheaf admits a finite locally closed stratification on each piece $Z$ of which it is pro-etale locally a cokernel $(A_T^c|_Z)^m\to(A_T^c|_Z)^n$, for finite $m,n\geq0$ [def-constructible-stratification]. For $F=E_T\otimes^L_{B_T}-$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the inverse encoding $D(\Phi_E)^{-1}F(K)$ belongs to the archived category $\mathcal C_T^c(E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], with precisely its bounded stratified local-finite-presentation condition. Moreover $\mathcal C_T^c(E)$ is a full triangulated subcategory of the ambient internal module derived category, with its induced shift and distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. No torsion-freeness or local freeness of the integral cohomology modules is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the coefficient comparison from the existing projection-normalized completed-ring comparison and the limiting continuous residue cone. The norm of the specified normed algebra is the spectral norm, so the actual integral ring and the WithAbs integral ring have identical topologies and identical underlying elements. The explicit ULift section isomorphism and this topology identity give the final integral chart. Evaluate each finite residue projection; the coefficient ULift and discrete-continuous maps reduce the equation to the normalization of the limiting cone. No arbitrary witness for the coefficient object is chosen.

A section that is a unit in every stalk is a unit globally, giving the invertibility hypothesis of the integral stratified-perfect characterization. Apply its equivalences to the given completed object K, retaining its actual etale-origin property. It gives a global bound and finite completed constant models for every cohomology module. The inverse completed encoding is an additive equivalence, hence exact; it preserves the bound and commutes with cohomology. Apply the ordinary integral-model encoding lemma to each cohomology module, then transport constructibility along the exact-functor cohomology comparison.

Apply the ordinary scalar-encoding lemma to the chosen c. Write L for internal extension along the actual chart-conjugated integral inclusion. The lemma gives finite-limit preservation of L and the square pbcExtend(a) followed by the inverse field encoding is isomorphic to the inverse completed encoding followed by L. Exactness of the encodings and reflection by the inverse field equivalence imply finite-limit preservation of pbcExtend(a). It is a left adjoint, hence preserves finite colimits. Uniqueness of universal left-derived functors identifies pbcDerivedExtend(a) with the exact termwise functor; derive the ordinary square. The existing bounded-constructible exact-scalar-extension theorem applies to the integral image from the previous step. Finally identify the universal derived L with its exact termwise functor and transport this bounded-constructible property through the derived square. All comparisons concern the existing universal derived functors; no replacement derived functor is defined.

Use the generic proved helper in the condensed constructible Serre module, with the specified continuous field ring itself and the finite-free local presentation theorem for these coefficients. This supplies kernel, cokernel and extension closure without choosing an algebraic closure or an embedded intermediate field. Isomorphism closure is the existing instance. The existing bounded-constructible triangulation criterion then gives precisely the asserted full triangulated subcategory.

The target predicate is invariant under ring isomorphism, so the exact coherence of these identifications is not load-bearing. Step 2: the characterization's hypotheses (noetherian, finite-dimensional, ℓ a unit in local rings) and its (i) with etale-origin witnesses match I_T exactly. Choose a presentation of N, push it through the exact F_T, then use exact inverse image and slice restriction (local-derived-restriction-comparisons). Step 3: continuous-scalar-derived-encoding gives D(Φ_E)∘(E^c⊗A^c −) ≅ F∘D(Φ_A), exact and termwise. Inverse image is monoidal and preserves colimits, so the restricted tensor of a presentation is again a presentation. No local freeness is used. Step 4: take Ω to be an algebraic closure of E. It is algebraic over Q_ℓ by the tower law, a two-line argument for which no node exists; I accept it as elementary (advisory only). The topology on E matches by uniqueness of the extended absolute value. The Serre lemma's closure properties are exactly the hypotheses of prop-weil-pbc-module-bounded-constructible-triangulated with R=E_T^c, and its full subcategory is the archived C_T^c(E). Edge cases checked: empty T; K=A_T; K=A_T/ϖ^r, whose E-image is 0; m=0 or n=0. No cycle: the item is absent from the closure of its 17 dependencies.
